threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pay for your coffee with cash and look surprised when your change is in coins. Everyone else is using contactless like it's second nature.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last Saturday; saw a bloke trying to barter a kebab for a seat. Driver just shook his head and laughed.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The evening smell of grilled kebabs wafting from the corner stand while kids chase each other on the sidewalk, that’s when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find spontaneous open-air techno raves in abandoned buildings here; it's not just a party, it's a Berlin ritual.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their tolerance for BART delays—baffled tourists are still on their phones trying to figure out the next bus.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo on the 7 bus heading to a wedding. He said 'better late than never' as we all looked on. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas. In Gràcia, some of the best spots offer pintxos, and they're missing out by sticking to the familiar.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a newcomer by their confusion over which side of the street the tram stops on; locals glide right past without a second thought.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You walk into a pub and order a ‘pint’ without knowing you’re supposed to ask for a ‘lager’ or ‘bitter’ first. Instant giveaway.
Saw a guy on the 77 last night trying to pay with a half-eaten apple. The driver just stared, so he switched to a crumpled fiver. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I stumbled upon a random street festival—music blasting, food stalls from every culture, and everyone just vibing together.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you enjoy a currywurst at 3 AM after a night out, while a street musician plays techno on the corner.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s from here when they can name the exact taco truck that shuts down during BART delays, while newcomers are still just waiting for the N-Judah.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a tourist mistaking the Muni driver for an Uber. The driver just laughed, pointing to the sign. Classic Tenderloin confusion.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all locals hit up the plaça on weekends. Most of us avoid it like the plague—way too many selfie sticks.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the subway machines—always tapping their cards but missing the simple fact that you need to scan it on the way out.
